summary: I mapped the original Web Displays (montoyo, MC 1.12.2, v1.1). It has 142 Java files and 17,851 lines. The only parts the spawn screen ("telão") needs are the screen multiblock (BlockScreen, Multiblock, BlockSide, hit2pixels, TileEntityScreen), a narrow networking core, one TESR and a small slice of MCEF. About 70% of the code is optional: a JSON GUI framework (~5.0k lines), the miniserv file host (~2.1k lines), minePad, laser pointer, upgrades, the JS/redstone API, CC/OC interfaces and advancements. The design is server-authoritative for state only. The server stores URL, size, resolution, rotation, owner, rights and upgrades, and relays URL changes and input events (click, keys, laser, JS) to clients within a 64-block radius. Every client runs its own Chromium and decodes the video itself, so playback is never synchronized. Players who arrive later miss earlier clicks and keystrokes. Link navigation done on one client changes only that client (the code marks this with a FIXME). Audio bypasses Minecraft entirely: CEF plays it on the OS device, and the only distance volume is a YouTube-only JavaScript `setVolume` hack. The screen permission defaults let any player change the URL and click on a new screen. Each face is drawn as one immediate-mode GL quad textured with the MCEF texture ID; MCEF uploads BGRA dirty rectangles with glTexSubImage2D. The MCEF calls WD makes are few (createBrowser, resize, getTextureID, close, loadURL, runJS, isPageLoading, inject mouse/key, display handler, JS query handler, a scheme, punycode, mime type). Most map one-to-one onto CinemaMod MCEF 2.x (MCEFBrowser.sendMouse*/sendKey*/getRenderer().getTextureID()). The modern fork (Mysticpasta1/CinemaMod) did not solve sync. Its 1.20 branch has a cleaner ScreenControl registry. It keeps the navigation FIXME, turns off the JS relay, redstone output and distance volume, and drops the original 128-block range and remote-controller checks. The audio-handler branch routes CefAudioHandler PCM into Minecraft's OpenAL; its commit messages call it janky and about 43 packets late. The expirement/ssr branch is an unfinished prototype of a headless browser on the server with raw BGRA dirty-rect serialization and no network code. A third-party MIT mod for 1.20.1 (WebDisplaysTogether) has since built server-side rendering with VP8/VP9 and Opus. I found no public source for Web Displays 1.7.10 (0.8–0.11). The only public 1.7.10 browser code is MCEF 0.3/0.4 from January 2015, in the git history of montoyo/mcef. The deployed MCEF-1.7.10 0.7 jar pulls a 2015-era CEF build (it includes ffmpegsumo.dll). A GTNH mod (TeXTech) that uses that jar warns it often installs but will not start on GTNH/Prism, so it is not a viable base. The GTNH stack adds two problems I confirmed in Angelica's code. Angelica redirects mod GL calls, including glBegin and glBindTexture, into GLStateManager. It also caches each tile entity's render bounds per class, which will cull a multiblock screen whose bounds grow after creation unless the screen is registered as a dynamic-bounds class. On 1.7.10, packet handlers already run on the main thread, and the in-house AkashicFM notes say SimpleNetworkWrapper must only send from the main thread. I estimate porting the must-have scope at 11–18 person-days on the WD side, plus 5–10 for a modern CEF binding on 1.7.10 with lwjgl3ify and Java 17+, against about 20 calendar days. The scope must be cut hard: telão-only build, admin-only input, locked navigation, a live-edge sync command, and distance-based volume first. Licensing allows a GTNH rewrite: WD is public domain (keep credit and headers), the fork is MIT (keep the notice), and CinemaMod MCEF is LGPL-2.1 (ship it as a separate library). Avoid copying montoyo's net.montoyo.mcef code, which has no licence grant.

findings.claim: montoyo/webdisplays is v1.12.2-1.1 on Forge 1.12.2-14.23.5.2768, 66 commits, 142 Java files / 17,851 lines; @Mod requires 'required-after:mcef@[1.0,2.0)'. Line counts per subsystem: client/gui 4,992 (JSON-driven custom GUI framework), miniserv 2,127, entity 2,111, net 1,648, utilities 1,403, block 987, item 822, core 755, renderers 689, ClientProxy 790, JSQueryDispatcher 370, WDScheme 149.

3 blocks. (1) BlockScreen: metadata bit0=hasTE, bit1=emitting (redstone output); 6 unlisted properties 'neighbor0..5' (0-15) give connected-texture borders through the custom baked model ScreenBaker, which uses sprites screen0..screen15. (2) BlockPeripheral: PropertyEnum type=DefaultPeripheral{KEYBOARD, CC_INTERFACE, OC_INTERFACE, REMOTE_CONTROLLER, REDSTONE_CONTROLLER, SERVER} plus facing 0-3 packed into metadata by DefaultPeripheral.toMetadata/fromMetadata. (3) BlockKeyboardRight: the second half of the 2-block keyboard.

TileEntityScreen exists only on the bottom-left origin block of the multiblock and holds up to 6 'Screen' records, one per face. Each record has side, size, resolution, rotation, url, videoType, owner, friends, friendRights, otherRights, upgrades (max 16), autoVolume, plus client-only browser, laserUser and server-only redstoneStatus. Peripheral TEs (via DefaultPeripheral.getTEClass): TileEntityKeyboard, TileEntityCCInterface, TileEntityOCInterface, TileEntityRCtrl (remote controller), TileEntityRedCtrl (redstone controller), TileEntityServer (miniserv host). TileEntityPeripheralBase stores the linked screen position and side in NBT.

Items: ItemScreenConfigurator (opens the config GUI: resolution, rotation, friends, rights, upgrades, auto-volume), ItemOwnershipThief, ItemLinker (links a peripheral to a screen), ItemMinePad2 (handheld browser with PadID/PadURL NBT; pad IDs persisted in <world>/wd_next.txt), ItemUpgrade (lasermouse, redinput, redoutput, gps), ItemLaserPointer, ItemCraftComponent (stonekey, upgrade, peripheral, batcell, batpack, laserdiode, backlight, extcard, badextcard), ItemMulti advancement icons. 6 SoundEvents (keyboardType, upgradeAdd, upgradeDel, screencfgOpen, server, ironic). 4 custom advancement criteria. A 'hard recipe' mode requires the pad_break advancement.

A right-click with an empty hand (or an upgrade item) on a face finds the origin by walking left, then down (Multiblock.findOrigin), measures up and right, and requires at least 2x2 and at most maxScreenSizeX/Y (default 16x16). Multiblock.check rejects holes, screen blocks directly in front of or behind the face, and screen blocks along the 4 edges. The TE is created by switching meta bit hasTE on the origin. Placing any screen block next to an existing screen destroys the neighbouring screens (onBlockPlacedBy). Sneak+right-click opens Set URL if the player has CHANGE_URL; a plain right-click becomes a click at hit2pixels coordinates.

One SimpleNetworkWrapper channel 'webdisplays' with 14 messages registered by reflection on @Message(messageId, side). Client-bound: 0 CMessageAddScreen, 3 CMessageOpenGui, 4 CMessageScreenUpdate, 6 CMessageACResult, 9 CMessageJSResponse, 11 CMessageMiniservKey, 12 CMessageServerInfo, 13 CMessageCloseGui. Server-bound: 1 SMessageRequestTEData, 2 SMessageScreenCtrl, 5 SMessageACQuery, 7 SMessagePadCtrl, 8 SMessageRedstoneCtrl, 10 SMessageMiniservConnect. Server handlers re-schedule onto WorldServer.addScheduledTask, which does not exist in 1.7.10.

findings.topic: Networking: what is synced server to client
findings.claim: Full state is sent by CMessageAddScreen: per screen side, size, url, resolution, rotation, owner and upgrades. It is NOT sending friends, friend/other rights or autoVolume, and the client comment says 'Since rights aren't synchronized, let the server check them'. A client TE asks for it in onLoad() via SMessageRequestTEData (server honours it within 512 blocks). Incremental updates use CMessageScreenUpdate actions URL, RESOLUTION, DELETE, MOUSE(click/down/move/up), TYPE, UPGRADES, JS_REDSTONE, OWNER, ROTATION, RUN_JS and AUTO_VOL, sent with sendToAllAround and a TargetPoint radius of 64 blocks. Mouse, type and JS events are fire-and-forget: they are not persisted and are not replayed to players who load the screen later.

findings.topic: Sync model: each client is its own browser
findings.claim: The server never renders. Every client creates its own MCEF browser lazily in the TESR the first time the screen is drawn, and loads the URL independently. There is no playback-time synchronization. When a page navigates client-side (a link click or SPA URL change), onAddressChange only rewrites the local copy of scr.url, marked '//FIXME: This is an invalid fix for something that CANNOT be fixed'. The 1.20 fork keeps the identical FIXME. Each client therefore drifts independently.

ScreenRights bits: CHANGE_URL=1 (also run JS), CLICK=2 (also type), MANAGE_FRIEND_LIST=4, MANAGE_OTHER_RIGHTS=8, MANAGE_UPGRADES=16, CHANGE_RESOLUTION=32. The owner gets ALL. New screens set BOTH friendRights and otherRights to DEFAULTS = CHANGE_URL|CLICK|MANAGE_UPGRADES|CHANGE_RESOLUTION, so by default any player can change the URL, click and type. SMessageScreenCtrl.runUnsafe checks dimension, a 128-block range (remote controller: player reach distance plus the REMOTE_CONTROLLER block type), then per-control rights. The JS redstone-output API is owner-only and needs the REDSTONE_OUTPUT upgrade.

ScreenRenderer (TileEntitySpecialRenderer): it returns early when the TE is unloaded by distance, disables standard item lighting and the lightmap, enables GL_TEXTURE_2D, and disables cull and blend. For each screen face it lazily calls createBrowser(applyBlacklist(url)) plus resize (width and height swapped for 90/270 degrees), translates to the multiblock centre, rotates by face, applies a 100 ms 'turn-on' scale, rotates by the screen rotation, then does glBindTexture(GL_TEXTURE_2D, browser.getTextureID()) and draws one glBegin(GL_QUADS) quad at z=0.505 of half-size (size*0.5-2/16) with V flipped. It ends with GlStateManager.bindTexture(0). isGlobalRenderer() returns true while loaded, because 'Minecraft's AABB-in-view-frustum checking is crappy'. The block frame uses ScreenBaker baked quads.

findings.topic: How the browser texture is produced
findings.claim: MCEF 1.12 CefRenderer uploads Chromium OSR frames on the GL thread: a full glTexImage2D on resize, otherwise glTexSubImage2D per dirty rect using GL_UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH/SKIP_PIXELS/SKIP_ROWS and EXTBgra.GL_BGRA_EXT. CinemaMod MCEF does the same in MCEFRenderer, using Minecraft's RenderSystem.

(a) Right-click: server-side hit2pixels maps the hit to browser pixels (handles rotation), then click() broadcasts MOUSE_CLICK to clients, which call injectMouseMove + injectMouseButton press/release. It is skipped while a laser user holds the lock. (b) Laser pointer: client raycasts 64 blocks, sends LASER_DOWN/MOVE (throttled to 100 ms) and LASER_UP. The server requires the CLICK right and the LASER_MOUSE upgrade, keeps one laser lock per screen, and broadcasts MOUSE_DOWN/MOVE/UP. (c) Keyboard peripheral: GuiKeyboard grabs the mouse and reads LWJGL2 Keyboard events into TypeData (PRESS/RELEASE/TYPE). It sends them as JSON every 5 ticks via SMessageScreenCtrl CTRL_TYPE; the server checks CLICK and broadcasts UPDATE_TYPE; clients call injectKeyPressedByKeyCode/ReleasedByKeyCode/injectKeyTyped. (d) The minePad GUI injects keys and mouse locally with no networking except the pad URL. The mouse wheel is never forwarded to in-world screens (injectMouseWheel is unused).

Forge Configuration with these keys. main: blacklist (domain list), padHeight=480, hardRecipes=true, homepage='mod://webdisplays/main.html', disableOwnershipThief=false, maxResolutionX/Y=1920/1080, miniservPort=25566 (0 disables), miniservQuota=1024 KiB, maxScreenSizeX/Y=16/16. client: loadDistance=30, unloadDistance=32 (forced to at least load+2). clientAutoVolume: enableAutoVolume=true, ytVolume=100, dist100=10, dist0=30. Default resolution per face is (blocks*16-4)*8 px, clamped to the max resolution. The domain blacklist is applied server-side on setScreenURL and client-side on navigation.

findings.topic: Mapping WD calls to CinemaMod MCEF 2.x
findings.claim: createBrowser maps to MCEF.createBrowser(url, transparent) or new MCEFBrowser(MCEF.getClient(), url, transp) + setCloseAllowed() + createImmediately(). Other mappings: resize→MCEFBrowser.resize; getTextureID→getRenderer().getTextureID(); injectMouseMove→sendMouseMove(x,y); injectMouseButton→sendMousePress/sendMouseRelease(x,y,button) with GLFW-style numbering (it swaps 1 and 2); injectKeyTyped→sendKeyTyped(char,mods); injectKey*ByKeyCode→sendKeyPress/sendKeyRelease(GLFW keyCode, scanCode, mods); injectMouseWheel→sendMouseWheel; runJS→CefBrowser.executeJavaScript; loadURL→CefBrowser.loadURL; isPageLoading→CefBrowser.isLoading; registerDisplayHandler→MCEF.getClient().addDisplayHandler(CefDisplayHandler); JS queries→CefMessageRouter on client.getHandle(); scheme→registerSchemeHandlerFactory; mime→MIMEUtil; punycode→java.net.IDN. draw() has no equivalent, so the caller draws the textured quad. CinemaMod's java-cef uses GLFW key codes, while WD on 1.7.10 under lwjgl3ify gets LWJGL2 Keyboard codes, so a mapping table is required.

master is a Forge 1.19.2 port (forge 1.19.2-43.2.10) on Mysticpasta1's mcef-forge fork. That last commit only added getCurrentTime/seekTo JS templates to VideoType, and in 1.20 their registration is commented out, so no sync shipped.

findings.claim: Intent: route Chromium audio into Minecraft's positional sound system. WDAudioHandler implements JCEF CefAudioHandler and is registered with MCEF.getClient().addAudioHandler. onAudioStreamPacket copies float PCM into a deque. WDAudioStream (a Minecraft AudioStream) converts it to 16-bit PCM for a looping, linearly attenuated WDAudioSource at the screen position. Mixins on com.mojang.blaze3d.audio.Channel change buffer size, pump count and the stop check. It uses a custom MCEF jar committed to libs (mcef-forge-2.1.5-1.20.1.jar). The author's own commit messages say 'audio handling works, but is ~43 audio packets delayed' and 'janky and wip audio stuff'. The branch is NOT merged into 1.20, which only carries an inert WDAudioSource stub.

findings.claim: Intent: server-side rendering (one browser on the server, pixels streamed to clients). It adds BrowserGen (chooses a client MCEFBrowser, or a RemoteBrowser when isSSR()), ServerBrowser extends a custom MCEFHeadlessBrowser, and ServerRenderer serializes raw BGRA dirty-rects (count, x, y, w, h, bytes) uncompressed. Also added: client RemoteBrowser/ImageReader to blit into an MCEFRenderer texture, S2CMessageEnableSSR, and a NetworkedBrowserTest. The commit message is 'ssr prototyping, no network logic hooked up yet' (2023-10-19), with no further commits. Uncompressed 1280x720x4 bytes is about 3.7 MB per full frame, so this design is not viable for video without a codec (INFERRED arithmetic).

findings.topic: Third-party completion of the SSR idea
findings.claim: He-Horatio/WebDisplaysTogether (MIT, created 2026-07-26) runs the page in headless Chromium on the server and streams VP8/VP9 video and Opus audio at 30 fps, 360p–1080p adaptive, so 'every player sees the identical frame'. It targets Forge 1.20.1 / Fabric and NeoForge 1.21.1, needs MCEF 2.1.1+ on client and server plus Java 17, and bundles FFmpeg natives (LGPL). Dedicated Linux servers need Chromium libraries and Xvfb. It is a design reference only, not 1.7.10 code.

Hi 64 bits'), then 0.11 for 1.7.10 ('Now using MCEF'). Versions 0.2–0.4 used Awesomium. The thread's document carries 'Copyright © 2013 Nicolas BARBOTIN ... may not be reproduced ... except for personal, private use'. montoyo.net's WD download page now offers only 1.12.2 and 1.10.2. findings.claim: Angelica (HEAD 3389b95, 2026-10-04) bytecode-redirects GL calls in mod classes (glEnable/Disable, glBegin, glBindTexture, ...) to GLStateManager. Core exclusions are only 'org.lwjgl', 'com.gtnewhorizon.gtnhlib.asm', 'com.gtnewhorizons.angelica.glsm.' and 'me.eigenraven.lwjgl3ify'. glBegin/glVertex/glEnd are emulated through ImmediateModeRecorder into a DirectTessellator draw. Its public GLRedirects javadoc says redirection exists 'for state tracking and core profile compatibility' and that code bypassing class transformation (reflection, MethodHandles, script engines) must redirect itself. So WD's raw GL in the TESR is redirected, but GL calls in a CEF binding loaded outside LaunchClassLoader would bypass the state cache.

Angelica overwrites TileEntity.getRenderBoundingBox. It classifies each TE class once as STATIC, INFINITE or DYNAMIC by calling getRenderBoundingBox on the first instance, and caches each TE's AABB keyed on (x, y, z, block, metadata). STATIC TEs are culled with the cached box, and chunk meshing treats them as section-local unless the AABB leaves the section. Only class names listed in AngelicaConfig.dynamicBoundsTileEntities (RequiresMcRestart) or passed to TileEntityRenderBoundsRegistry.registerDynamicClass are re-evaluated live. WD's screen TE starts with a 1x1 box and grows it in updateAABB() after a screen is added, which is exactly the pattern this cache gets wrong.

findings.topic: 1.7.10 idioms confirmed in local GTNH code
findings.claim: Confirmed 1.7.10 equivalents in local code: TESR renderTileEntityAt(TileEntity,double,double,double,float); TE sync via getDescriptionPacket()/onDataPacket(S35PacketUpdateTileEntity) plus markBlockForUpdate; canUpdate(); shouldRefresh(Block,Block,int,int,World,int,int,int); onBlockActivated(World,int,int,int,EntityPlayer,int side,float,float,float); registerBlockIcons(IIconRegister)/getIcon; GameRegistry.registerBlock(block, ItemBlockClass, name) and registerTileEntity(Class,String); SimpleNetworkWrapper and ByteBufUtils under cpw.mods.fml; ctx.getServerHandler().playerEntity; sounds.json in the same format plus world.playSoundEffect; MinecraftForgeClient.registerItemRenderer; @SideOnly from cpw.mods.fml.relauncher.

AkashicFM documents that on 1.7.10 mod packets go through the vanilla queue and handlers run on the main thread, so WD's addScheduledTask indirection is unnecessary. It also says SimpleNetworkWrapper stores the destination in shared channel attributes, so sending from two threads can swap recipients and only the main thread may send. WD/MCEF callbacks such as onAddressChange (which sends SMessagePadCtrl) and CEF JS queries must therefore be queued to the client tick before sending.

BlockPos/IBlockState/EnumFacing become int x,y,z, getBlock/getBlockMetadata/setBlockMetadataWithNotify and int side (0-5). WD's BlockSide enum order BOTTOM, TOP, NORTH, SOUTH, WEST, EAST already matches 1.7.10 side indices. WD's own Vector3i/Vector2i/BlockSide/Multiblock/hit2pixels/Rotation math is engine-independent and ports almost verbatim; only toBlock()/MutableBlockPos helpers change. The hasTE/emitting state is already a 2-bit metadata encoding. ExtendedBlockState plus the baked model for connected borders becomes getIcon(IBlockAccess,x,y,z,side) over 16 IIcons reusing screen0..15.png. EnumHand/ItemStack.isEmpty/shrink become getCurrentEquippedItem/null/stackSize--. Effort: ~1–1.5 person-days for screen block plus multiblock.

findings.claim: TileEntity.onLoad() (client data request plus screen tracking) does not exist in 1.7.10. Replace SMessageRequestTEData + CMessageAddScreen(full) with getDescriptionPacket/onDataPacket carrying the Screen NBT, and register tracking in validate()/first render. ITickable is not used by the screen TE, so canUpdate() can return false. shouldRefresh must keep the TE when only the emitting bit changes. RegistryEvent.Register<Block/Item/SoundEvent> becomes GameRegistry.registerBlock/registerItem in preInit plus sounds.json names. GameRegistry.registerTileEntity takes a String. The capability (WDDCapability, only a first-run flag) becomes player persisted NBT or IExtendedEntityProperties. Advancements/CriteriaTriggers have no equivalent (drop, or use Achievements). Effort for the TileEntityScreen core: ~1–1.5 person-days.

render(T,x,y,z,partialTicks,destroyStage,alpha) becomes renderTileEntityAt(TileEntity,x,y,z,partialTicks). isGlobalRenderer() does not exist in 1.7.10; vanilla culls TESRs by getRenderBoundingBox and getMaxRenderDistanceSquared (default 64 blocks), and Angelica adds its own bounds cache, so a large screen must return a correct full-multiblock AABB from the moment the TE exists, or INFINITE_EXTENT_AABB, plus Angelica dynamic registration. setLightmapDisabled and GlStateManager become OpenGlHelper.setActiveTexture(lightmapTexUnit) and GL11 calls, which Angelica redirects. Draw the quad with Tessellator.instance (startDrawingQuads/addVertexWithUV) rather than glBegin. Effort: ~1.5–2.5 person-days including Angelica testing.

findings.claim: The package moves net.minecraftforge.fml.common.network → cpw.mods.fml.common.network (SimpleNetworkWrapper, IMessage, IMessageHandler, ByteBufUtils, NetworkRegistry.TargetPoint, sendToAllAround all exist). Remove WorldServer.addScheduledTask and Minecraft.addScheduledTask, since handlers already run on the main thread. Use ctx.getServerHandler().playerEntity. The reflective @Message registration in Messages.registerAll ports unchanged. The telão needs only a subset (state sync, SetURL, Click, Type, Resolution/Rotation, a new SyncLiveEdge and Lock). findings.topic: Portability: client input, GUIs, sounds, items
findings.claim: org.lwjgl.input.Keyboard/Mouse is LWJGL2 API, which 1.7.10 uses natively and lwjgl3ify emulates; key codes must be mapped to whatever the CEF binding expects (AWT VK in old MCEF via remapKeycode, GLFW codes in CinemaMod java-cef). The custom JSON GUI framework (~5k lines) depends on 1.12 GuiScreen/BufferBuilder/fontRenderer names: a full port is 3–4 person-days, whereas the telão needs only a 1-field Set URL GUI plus a keyboard-capture GUI (~1 person-day). RenderSpecificHandEvent (minePad/laser in hand) becomes the IItemRenderer EQUIPPED_FIRST_PERSON route. SoundEvent objects become string names with world.playSoundEffect. Raycast uses Vec3.createVectorHelper and world.rayTraceBlocks.

jcefmaven's pom compiles with maven.compiler.source/target 8 and the README says 'supports Java 8+', but on JDK 16+ it requires --add-opens/--add-exports for java.desktop/sun.awt, sun.lwawt, sun.java2d and java.base/java.lang. These flags matter on lwjgl3ify's Java 17–25 clients.

findings.topic: Live latency of the stream source
findings.claim: YouTube's own documentation: with Low latency most viewers see under 10 s, with Ultra-low latency under 5 s (Normal is higher). The broadcaster chooses this setting, not the viewer. A per-client Chromium inherits that delay plus its own buffering, so 'almost no ms' is not achievable against real time. Between players, the skew equals each client's distance from the live edge, typically seconds, unless the server periodically pushes everyone to the live edge (INFERRED).

findings.topic: Known WD problems from issue trackers
findings.claim: montoyo/webdisplays issues, by comments: '[1.12.2] White Screen' #15 (42), white-screen variants #102, #180, #150, #124, #166, #146, #154; codec problems 'Attention for people who suffer from codecs!' #114, 'H.264 Videos don't seem to work' #27, WebM #106/#79; 'Optifine lightning problem' #2; 'Sync [suggestion]' #44 (closed, no maintainer reply). CinemaMod/webdisplays: 'Screens are not syncronised with other players' #28 (open), 'If the browser block is in use when entering the game, it may cause the game to crash' #100, '[1.20.1] Screen will not turn off based on distance' #6, 'Still hearing a YouTube video after deleting the world' #11, 'Minepad screen flicking' #92.

A full 1920x1080 BGRA frame is 8,294,400 bytes, so a fully changing video at 30 fps uploads about 249 MB/s per client through glTexSubImage2D on the render thread, on top of Chromium's own decode. 1280x720 is about 110 MB/s. WD's default for a 16x9-block face would be (16*16-4)*8 = 2016 px wide, clamped to 1920.

montoyo/webdisplays LICENSE: 'This mod and its source code is now in public domain. Feel free to do whatever you want with it; make forks, distribute it... whatever I would appreciate it, of course, if you credited me'. The README repeats that anyone may fork or redistribute. Source files still carry 'Copyright (C) 2018/2019 BARBOTIN Nicolas' headers. Bundled assets include jQuery 3.3.1 (MIT header). A GTNH rewrite may reuse, relicense and redistribute WD code. Keeping credit and headers is prudent because public-domain dedications are not recognized identically in every jurisdiction (INFERRED). The 'ironic.ogg' meme sound has unknown provenance and should not be shipped (INFERRED).

findings.topic: License: modern fork, MCEF variants, JCEF
findings.claim: Mysticpasta1/CinemaMod webdisplays: MIT 'Copyright (c) 2023 CinemaMod Group', so code can be copied if the MIT notice is kept. CinemaMod MCEF: LGPL-2.1, so it can be used as a separate library from an MIT/PD mod; modifications to MCEF itself must be published under LGPL, and shading it into the mod jar brings the LGPL relinking obligations (INFERRED reading). montoyo MCEF: its LICENSE grants BSD-3 (JCEF terms) only for the org.cef package and the native folder, and the net.montoyo.mcef.* code carries no licence grant, so do not copy it (INFERRED legal effect). Its README asks 'please not a WebDisplays clone'. TeXTech-GTNH and WebDisplaysTogether are MIT (WebDisplaysTogether bundles LGPL FFmpeg).

problems.name: Old MCEF 1.7.10 is not a viable browser base
problems.root_cause: The only 1.7.10 MCEF is a closed 0.7 jar with 2015-era CEF (resource set 0.6, ffmpegsumo.dll) plus 0.3/0.4 source from Jan 2015. It adds natives through ClassLoader.usr_paths reflection, and both montoyo.net and TeXTech warn that it fails with modern launchers and on GTNH/Prism.
problems.fix: Do not build on MCEF 1.7.10. Put a thin 'IWebView' adapter (createBrowser, resize, textureId, close, loadURL, executeJS, mouse/key/wheel, onAddressChange, JS query) between the WD port and a modern CEF binding (CinemaMod java-cef/MCEF core or jcefmaven, Java 8 bytecode). Use explicit native download with SHA-256 verification, reusing AkashicFM's ToolManager pattern. Prototype this first (days 1–5), because everything else depends on it.

problems.name: Anyone can change the URL or click on a new screen
problems.root_cause: addScreen sets friendRights and otherRights to ScreenRights.DEFAULTS (CHANGE_URL|CLICK|MANAGE_UPGRADES|CHANGE_RESOLUTION), and CHANGE_URL also allows running JS through computer interfaces.
problems.fix: Add a server-side 'telão lock' flag: otherRights=friendRights=NONE. Gate SetURL, Click, Type, Resolution and SyncLiveEdge on an OP permission level or an Akashic admin list, and keep the original dimension and 128-block checks. Add a server URL allowlist (scheme https, allowed hosts such as youtube.com/youtu.be). Log every admin action to an audit log as AkashicFM does.

problems.name: Client-side navigation desyncs screens
problems.root_cause: onAddressChange → updateClientSideURL only rewrites the local scr.url (FIXME 'CANNOT be fixed'), so a link click, redirect, pop-up or YouTube SPA navigation on one client is never reflected on the server or on other clients. The 1.20 fork keeps the same FIXME.
problems.fix: In telão-lock mode, cancel any navigation whose URL is outside the server URL's allowlist and same-page scope (JCEF CefRequestHandler.onBeforeBrowse or the display-handler callback, then loadURL(serverUrl)); block pop-ups. In unlocked mode, have the admin's client report navigation to the server as a SetURL, queued to the main thread and rate-limited, so the server rebroadcasts.

problems.name: No playback sync between players (each client its own Chromium)
problems.root_cause: The architecture replicates only URL and input events. Each client buffers the live stream independently and joins at a different time, and there is no time-sync code. The fork's seekTo/getCurrentTime attempt is commented out and its SSR prototype is unfinished.
problems.fix: Add a whitelisted server command 'SYNC_LIVE_EDGE' (not arbitrary JS), broadcast every N seconds and on join. It runs a fixed script that seeks the main <video> to seekable.end - offset, or the YouTube player API equivalent. Choose a YouTube source with Ultra-low latency (<5 s by Google's docs). State plainly that the target is seconds, not milliseconds. Full server-side rendering (as in WebDisplaysTogether) is out of scope for 20 days on 1.7.10.

problems.name: Late joiners miss clicks; unattended autoplay
problems.root_cause: Mouse and key events are broadcast once to players within 64 blocks and never persisted. A player who loads the screen later gets only the URL, so a video started by an admin click never starts for them. Chromium also blocks unmuted autoplay without a user gesture (INFERRED from Chromium autoplay policy).
problems.fix: Make the telão self-starting: an autoplay-capable URL, the CEF command-line switch --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required set by the port's CEF init (to be validated on the chosen binding), and the SYNC_LIVE_EDGE command on join. Keep server-side 'last state' (URL plus playing flag) inside the description packet.

problems.name: Update radius smaller than useful view distance
problems.root_cause: All updates use TargetPoint radius 64 (point()). If loadDistance is raised for a big spawn screen, clients between 64 blocks and loadDistance keep a live browser but miss URL, rotation and sync updates.
problems.fix: For the telão, send updates to all players in the dimension (or those tracking the chunk plus a margin at least equal to the configured loadDistance). Use the same set for SYNC_LIVE_EDGE.

problems.name: Audio not integrated with Minecraft
problems.root_cause: CEF plays audio on the OS device, so it is not positional, ignores Minecraft volume sliders, and keeps playing if the browser is not closed. The only distance volume is a YouTube-only JS setVolume, with FIXME 'Not called if enableSoundDistance is false'; 1.20 commented it out entirely. The fork's PCM-to-OpenAL branch reports about 43 packets of delay and is unmerged.
problems.fix: MVP: a per-tick, distance-based volume that multiplies Minecraft master and records volume, applied by a generic script to every <video>/<audio> (not only YouTube). Mute and close the browser on unload, world unload and disconnect. Stage 2: a CefAudioHandler (available in CinemaMod MCEFClient.addAudioHandler) feeding AkashicFM's OpenAL streaming source with EFX, plus a jitter buffer.

problems.name: Angelica render-bounds cache culls the multiblock
problems.root_cause: Angelica classifies TE classes and caches each TE's AABB keyed on position, block and metadata. WD's screen TE starts at 1x1 and grows the box later in updateAABB(). 1.7.10 also lacks isGlobalRenderer and limits TESRs to the default max render distance. The big screen can be culled whenever its origin block is off-frustum, or beyond 64 blocks.
problems.fix: Have getRenderBoundingBox return the full multiblock box computed from server data before first render, or INFINITE_EXTENT_AABB for the telão. Call com.gtnewhorizons.angelica.rendering.TileEntityRenderBoundsRegistry.registerDynamicClass(TileEntityScreen.class.getName()) reflectively at client init (soft dependency), or document adding the class to Angelica's dynamicBoundsTileEntities. Override getMaxRenderDistanceSquared to cover the plaza.

problems.name: GL state coherence with Angelica (immediate mode and foreign texture IDs)
problems.root_cause: WD draws with glBegin/glEnd and binds the CEF texture ID with raw GL11 calls. Angelica redirects these into GLStateManager (immediate mode becomes emulated tessellation), but any CEF renderer class loaded outside LaunchClassLoader, or excluded (e.g. org.lwjgl.*), would change texture bindings behind the cache. Angelica documents core-profile compatibility as a goal.
problems.fix: Draw with Tessellator.instance, bind via GL11 calls inside mod classes (redirected), and do the CEF texture upload inside the mod's own (transformed) renderer class on the render thread, not inside an excluded library. Save and restore state around the draw. Test with Angelica on and off, shaders on and off, and the GTNH 2.8 and 2.9 configs.

problems.name: Unsafe packet sending from non-main threads on 1.7.10
problems.root_cause: 1.7.10 SimpleNetworkWrapper keeps the destination in shared channel attributes, so sending from two threads can misroute. CEF callbacks (address change, JS queries) and miniserv threads in WD may send packets.
problems.fix: Route every send through a main-thread queue drained in ClientTickEvent/ServerTickEvent, and drop WD's addScheduledTask usage (handlers already run on the main thread in 1.7.10).

problems.name: Proprietary-codec streams show white or black screens
problems.root_cause: Standard CEF builds lack proprietary codecs, so H.264/AAC HLS streams (common for TV broadcasters) fail. The WD trackers have long-running codec and white-screen issues (#114, #27, #15, #102).
problems.fix: Choose and test the actual broadcast source by ~Oct 15. Prefer YouTube (served to Chromium as VP9/AV1 plus Opus, INFERRED) and confirm embedding or watch-page playback in the chosen CEF build. Keep a second allowlisted YouTube live URL as a fallback that admins can switch to with one command.

problems.name: Fork regression: lost range and remote checks
problems.root_cause: The 1.20 redesign's C2SMessageScreenCtrl.handle has no distance check, and SetURLControl has 'TODO: deal with remote', unlike the original runUnsafe, which checked dimension, a 128-block range, remote-controller reach and block type.
problems.fix: When borrowing the 1.20 ScreenControl registry design, re-add the original checks plus per-player rate limits and length caps on URL, text and JSON (Gson TypeData parse in type()).

problems.name: Miniserv opens an extra public TCP port
problems.root_cause: WD starts miniserv on world load, bound to InetSocketAddress(port) with default port 25566 (all interfaces), and tells clients about it on login.
problems.fix: Do not port miniserv, the server block or the wd:// scheme for the telão. If ever needed, default to miniservPort=0 and use vanilla networking.

problems.name: Client cost: full-res OSR upload and decode on every player
problems.root_cause: Each client decodes and uploads frames. At 1080p30 that is about 249 MB/s of glTexSubImage2D (INFERRED arithmetic), and WD's default resolution for a big face clamps to 1920 wide. Low-end GTNH clients will lose FPS near spawn.
problems.fix: Fix the telão at 1280x720 with a capped windowless frame rate of 30. Pause frame upload when the screen is off-frustum or beyond loadDistance (close the browser beyond unloadDistance as WD does). Add a client config toggle 'hide telão' that shows a static poster instead.

problems.name: Client crashes when the browser is unavailable
problems.root_cause: ClientProxy.postInit throws RuntimeException('MCEF is missing') when the API is null. CinemaMod issue #100 reports a crash when entering a world with a screen in use.
problems.fix: Degrade gracefully: if CEF fails to initialize (missing natives, unsupported OS), render a placeholder texture with a message and keep the client playable. Never hard-crash on join.

problems.name: Key-code mismatch for admin typing
problems.root_cause: WD captures LWJGL2 Keyboard codes (lwjgl3ify emulates the LWJGL2 API). Old MCEF remapped only about 13 special keys to AWT VK codes; CinemaMod java-cef expects GLFW key codes and scancodes.
problems.fix: Add an explicit LWJGL2→GLFW (or →VK) mapping table in the adapter and send TYPE events for characters. Test accents for pt-BR (ABNT2 dead keys) on Windows and Linux.

problems.name: License hygiene when mixing sources
problems.root_cause: WD is public domain, the fork is MIT, CinemaMod MCEF is LGPL-2.1, and montoyo's net.montoyo.mcef code has no licence grant. Assets include jQuery (MIT) and a meme sound of unknown origin.
problems.fix: Reuse WD and fork code with credit, keeping the PD headers and the MIT notice. Use CinemaMod MCEF or JCEF as separate, unmodified-or-published LGPL/BSD libraries. Do not copy net.montoyo.mcef.* or redistribute old WD and MCEF jars. Drop ironic.ogg. Record SHA-256 of any native bundle per Akashic rules.

problems.name: Schedule risk: about 16–28 person-days of work in about 20 calendar days
problems.root_cause: The must-have WD port is estimated at 11–18 person-days plus 5–10 for the 1.7.10 CEF binding, with QA on several Java and GTNH versions, before Sunday 2026-10-25 17:00 BRT.
problems.fix: Build a telão-only product first: one screen block, admin-locked, SetURL plus SYNC_LIVE_EDGE plus JS distance volume, no peripherals, upgrades, minePad, laser or GUI framework. Order of work: CEF spike in days 1–5, then the WD core port, a feature freeze around Oct 18, a public rehearsal with real players around Oct 20–22 on the actual live channel, and a go/no-go by Oct 23. Keep a clearly labelled safety net ready (e.g. AkashicFM audio relay of the same broadcast) in case clients cannot run CEF.

open_questions: Which CEF binding will the 1.7.10 port use (CinemaMod java-cef fork, jcefmaven or another), which Chromium version does it ship, and do its Java classes load through LaunchClassLoader so Angelica's GL redirection covers its texture upload?

Does GTNH 2.8.x/2.9 with default Angelica settings run a GL core profile? Angelica's GLRedirects javadoc names core-profile compatibility; if so, raw or immediate-mode GL outside transformed classes would fail.

What exact source will carry the 2026-10-25 runoff coverage (which YouTube channel or broadcaster)? Is embedding or watch-page playback allowed, which latency mode does the broadcaster use, and is it H.264-only HLS (which would fail on a standard CEF build)?

Which client platforms does the community use (Windows, Linux, macOS Intel or ARM)? This decides the CEF native downloads per platform; the old MCEF 1.7.10 set alone was ~283.8 MiB for three platforms.

Must every player install the mod and CEF natives to join (1.7.10 FML registry sync with a new block)? Or should the mod be client-optional, with the screen block registered so that clients without CEF still connect and see a placeholder?
Who counts as admin for the telão (OP level, an Akashic permission list, specific UUIDs), and should URL changes need two-person confirmation during the live event?

Does 'almost no ms' mean delay relative to the TV broadcast (bounded by the broadcaster's YouTube latency mode) or skew between players (seconds without a sync command)? If Gabriel streams his own client via OBS, his viewers only see his client, so inter-player skew does not matter for them.
Do clients run Angelica/Iris shader packs? WD's full-bright quad (lightmap disabled, blend off) has not been tested under shaders on 1.7.10.
Not run: no build, client launch or GTNH test was executed in this research; every 1.7.10 behaviour above is from code reading, not from a live observation.
